defences.name: NCICD Phase A coastal wall (Muara Baru, Kalibaru)
defences.src: detikFinance, 4 Nov 2024 (Minister AHY); Berita Jakarta, 6 Sep 2017

impacts.text: Measured land subsidence in Jakarta ranged from about 1 to 15 centimetres a year, and up to 20 to 28 centimetres in a few places.
impacts.src: Abidin et al. (2011), Land subsidence of Jakarta (Indonesia) and its relation with urban development, Natural Hazards 59

impacts.text: Typical subsidence rates of 3 to 10 centimetres a year; several coastal areas now flood at high tide, mostly where the ground sinks fastest.
impacts.src: Abidin et al. (2015), Environmental impacts of land subsidence in urban areas of Indonesia, PIAHS 370

profile.text: A 2022 law makes Nusantara, on Borneo, the new capital, but Jakarta remains the capital until the President signs the decree on the move, as the Constitutional Court confirmed in May 2026.
profile.src: Mahkamah Konstitusi, ruling 71/PUU-XXIV/2026, reported by ANTARA (13 May 2026)

profile.text: DKI Jakarta had 10.7 million residents in the 2025 inter-census population survey (SUPAS).
profile.src: BPS DKI Jakarta, SUPAS 2025, reported by ANTARA (6 May 2026)

defences.name: TCAP raised land platform, Fongafale (Funafuti)
defences.datum: Chart Datum (design report: 5.8 m above tide gauge zero)
defences.basis: 2.4 m above contemporary HAT; flood-free for at least 80 years

impacts.text: Under the Australia–Tuvalu Falepili Union mobility pathway up to 280 Tuvaluans a year may move to Australia; more than 100 people had moved by April 2026.
impacts.src: Australian High Commission Tuvalu (16 Apr 2026)

impacts.text: Projections cited by the Green Climate Fund say daily high tides could cover half of Funafuti by 2050 and 95% of its land by 2100 under high sea-level scenarios (UNDP: 2050-2060, worst case).
impacts.src: Green Climate Fund (6 May 2025; TCAP funder)

impacts.text: The average height of land in Tuvalu is only about 0.5 m above high tide according to the TCAP elevation survey.
impacts.src: Green Climate Fund (6 May 2025; TCAP funder)

impacts.text: The Tuvalu Coastal Adaptation Project built 7.3 ha of raised storm-resilient land on Funafuti at a total cost of USD 38.9 million.
impacts.src: Green Climate Fund (6 May 2025; TCAP funder)

storms.name: Hurricane Sandy
storms.src: NOAA CO-OPS water level (6-min) and datums, station 8518750

impacts.text: Relative sea level at The Battery has risen about 2.95 mm a year since 1856, roughly 0.37 m since 1900 on a linear trend.
impacts.src: NOAA CO-OPS sea level trends station 8518750

impacts.text: IPCC AR6 finds it likely that the global proportion of major (Category 3–5) tropical cyclones has increased over the last four decades (disputed by some later analyses).
impacts.src: IPCC AR6 WGI SPM A.3.4 (errata 21 Oct 2021)

impacts.text: Sandy killed 44 people in New York City, displaced 35,000 residents and caused $19 billion in damage and lost economic activity.
impacts.src: NYC Mayor's Office of Climate and Environmental Justice, 'Sandy 10 Years Later' (Oct 2022), p. 3

impacts.text: Sandy flooded 51 square miles of New York City, 17 % of its land area, with nearly 90,000 buildings in the inundation zone.
impacts.src: NYC Mayor's Office of Climate and Environmental Justice, 'Sandy 10 Years Later' (Oct 2022), p. 3

impacts.text: About $8.1bn (5–95%: $4.7–14.0bn) of Sandy's more than $60bn damage is attributable to human-caused sea-level rise which also spread the flood to 71000 more people.

profile.text: About 400,000 New Yorkers lived in the 1%-annual-chance floodplain in 2016, more than live in Cleveland, Tampa or St. Louis.
profile.src: NYC Planning, Flood Risk in NYC (info brief, November 2016)

profile.text: New York City had an estimated 8.6 million residents in 2025.
profile.src: NYC Department of City Planning, Population Estimates and Trends, March 2026 (Census Bureau Vintage 2025)

defences.name: Public flood defence line (103 km of dikes and walls)
defences.basis: Design water level 7.30 m NHN at St. Pauli (before 2012); raised to 8.10 m NHN in 2012
defences.status: built; being raised by at least 0.80 m to about 2050
defences.src: LSBG Bericht Nr. 7, Hochwasserschutz in Hamburg - Anleitung Deichverteidigung, 2nd ed., p. 4

impacts.text: The February 1962 storm flood killed 315 people in Hamburg and flooded one sixth of the city; St. Pauli peaked at 5.70 m NN.
impacts.src: Freie und Hansestadt Hamburg BUKEA Sturmflut-Chronik

impacts.text: Hamburg raised its design water level from 7.30 to 8.10 m NHN; the 103 km public defence line is being raised by at least 80 cm by 2050.
impacts.src: Freie und Hansestadt Hamburg (Katastrophenschutz FAQ)

impacts.text: About 45 percent of Hamburg's area lies in storm-flood-prone lowland behind roughly 100 km of defences.
impacts.src: Freie und Hansestadt Hamburg BUKEA (Ellerholz project page)

impacts.text: The highest storm surge ever measured in Hamburg reached 6.45 m NHN at St. Pauli on 3 January 1976.
impacts.src: Freie und Hansestadt Hamburg Katastrophenschutz FAQ

profile.text: 1.87 million people lived in Hamburg at the end of 2025.
Its port handled 8.3 million containers (TEU) in 2025.
profile.src: Hamburg Port Authority, throughput figures 2025 (19 Feb 2026)

name: Mekong Delta: Ben Tre and Tra Vinh

defences.name: Ba Lai sluice-dam (Ben Tre)
defences.datum: probably national datum (Hon Dau); not stated
defences.src: vi.wikipedia, Cong dap Ba Lai (citing vncold.vn)

impacts.text: The 2020 salinity intrusion potentially damaged about 30,000 hectares of rice in Ca Mau.
impacts.src: Park et al. (2022), Ambio 51

impacts.text: By 7 March 2020 five Mekong Delta provinces had declared a state of emergency over drought and saltwater intrusion affecting all 13 delta provinces.
impacts.src: UN Viet Nam Flash Update No. 3 (25 Mar 2020)

impacts.text: In the 2019-20 dry season saltwater intrusion rose in 10 of the 13 delta provinces, leaving 96,000 households (430,000 people) short of water and harming 58,000 ha of rice (UN Viet Nam: 38,800 ha lost by 7 March 2020).
impacts.src: Duong et al. 2025 iScience 28:112723, p. 3 (citing earlier reporting)

impacts.text: More than half of the Mekong Delta's 600-kilometre shoreline was eroding between 2003 and 2012.
impacts.src: Anthony et al. (2015), Scientific Reports 5

impacts.text: Groundwater pumping alone makes the Mekong Delta sink by about 1.1 centimetres a year on average, and by more than 2.5 centimetres in places.
impacts.src: Minderhoud et al. (2017), Environmental Research Letters 12

profile.text: Since June 2025, Ben Tre and Tra Vinh belong to the merged province of Vinh Long, home to 4.3 million people.
profile.src: National Assembly of Viet Nam, Resolution 202/2025/QH15, Art. 1(20)

profile.text: The Mekong Delta grows about half of Viet Nam's rice and supplies about 95% of its rice exports.
profile.src: Voice of Vietnam (15 Sep 2024), citing Ministry of Industry and Trade statistics

impacts.text: Cyclone Aila killed 190 people in Bangladesh in May 2009, according to the Disaster Management Bureau.
impacts.src: Gupta 2009, Natural Hazards Center quick response report, p. 8, citing Bangladesh Disaster Management Bureau (2009)

impacts.text: Cyclone Amphan triggered about 2.5 million displacements in Bangladesh in 2020, mostly pre-emptive evacuations, the highest number recorded since 2008.
impacts.src: IDMC 2026 Disaster displacement risk in Bangladesh, p. 8 (CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO)

impacts.text: Disasters caused 21.2 million displacements in Bangladesh from 2008 to 2024, 11.3 million of them from cyclones and storm surges; these include pre-emptive evacuations.
impacts.src: IDMC (2026), Bangladesh: Disaster displacement risk profile

impacts.text: Salt-affected land in coastal Bangladesh grew from about 0.83 million hectares in 1973 to 1.06 million hectares in 2009.
impacts.src: SRDI survey, as reported in Salehin et al. (2018), Springer

profile.text: Shyamnagar, the subdistrict that includes the island of Gabura, had 366,000 people at the 2022 census.
profile.src: Bangladesh Bureau of Statistics, Census 2022, via citypopulation.de

profile.text: Next to it lies the Sundarbans, the largest continuous mangrove forest in the world; its Bangladeshi part has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1997.
profile.src: IUCN World Heritage Outlook, The Sundarbans (2025)

defences.name: Rosetta promontory seawall
defences.datum: 'above sea level' (probably Egyptian survey datum, near MSL; not stated)
defences.status: built (1990/1991; 1.5 km west, 3.5 km east of the mouth)
defences.src: Parlmany, 23 Sep 2016 (Ministry of Water Resources and Irrigation / Shore Protection Authority)

impacts.text: More than 280 buildings along Alexandria's shoreline collapsed in two decades as seawater intrusion weakened their foundations; more than 7,000 are at risk.
impacts.src: Fouad, Heggy et al. (2025), Earth's Future 13

impacts.text: With 0.44 m of sea-level rise plus measured subsidence a bathtub model puts 2660 km² of the northern delta below sea level by 2100 (defences not modelled).
impacts.src: Gebremichael et al. 2018 JGR Solid Earth doi:10.1002/2017JB015084

impacts.text: InSAR shows the northern Nile Delta sinking 2.4 mm a year on average and up to 9.7 mm a year over gas fields and groundwater pumping areas.
impacts.src: Gebremichael et al. 2018 JGR Solid Earth doi:10.1002/2017JB015084

impacts.text: Before the 1991 seawall the Rosetta promontory coast retreated on average 137.4 m a year.
impacts.src: Ghoneim et al. 2015 Geomorphology 228:1-14 doi:10.1016/j.geomorph.2014.08.021

profile.text: About half of Egypt's people live in or near the Nile Delta.
Alexandria, Egypt's second city, had about 5.5 million people in 2023.
The Aswan High Dam holds back more than 98% of the sediment that used to reach the delta.
profile.src: Gebremichael et al. 2018 (JGR Solid Earth), reported by Eos (24 Apr 2018)

defences.name: Larose to Golden Meadow ring levee (Lafourche)
defences.src: South Lafourche Levee District (listing on LouisianaLandCAN, updated Sep 2022)

impacts.text: The island shrank from more than 22,000 acres to about 320 acres.
impacts.src: Louisiana Office of Community Development, Isle de Jean Charles Resettlement

impacts.text: Coastal Louisiana lost about 4833 km² of land between 1932 and 2016, about 25% of its 1932 land area.
impacts.src: Couvillion et al. 2017 USGS SIM 3381 doi:10.3133/sim3381

impacts.text: The rate of land loss peaked at about 83.5 km² a year in the mid-1970s and has slowed to about 28 km² a year.
impacts.src: Couvillion et al. 2017 USGS SIM 3381 doi:10.3133/sim3381

impacts.text: Coastal Louisiana's land surface is sinking on average 9 ± 1 mm a year based on 274 CRMS monitoring sites.
impacts.src: Nienhuis et al. 2017 GSA Today 27(9) doi:10.1130/GSATG337GW.1

impacts.text: With $48 million from HUD, residents began moving to The New Isle near Schriever in August 2022; 37 households had moved by autumn 2024.
impacts.src: Louisiana Office of Community Development, Isle de Jean Charles Resettlement

profile.text: At recent rates the coast loses land the size of a football field about every 100 minutes.
Terrebonne and Lafourche parishes, home to Houma, Golden Meadow and Port Fourchon, had 207,000 residents at the 2020 census.
